{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows sustained negative sentiment (e.g., multiple -0.25 or 0.00 values), indicating market pessimism.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility in early periods (e.g., first 5-7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, as true outcomes often exhibit mean reversion toward prior levels.",
    "If model overestimates prices after a sharp spike (e.g., >70.00), apply a downward correction of 5-10% to avoid overshoot.",
    "When sentiment history includes a recent positive shift (e.g., 0.50 or 0.67), increase forecast sensitivity to recent price action, but cap upward adjustments to avoid overcorrection.",
    "For long-term forecasts (e.g., 30-day horizon), apply a smoothing filter to reduce noise from short-term sentiment fluctuations.",
    "If true outcome consistently deviates from forecast by >10% in the first 10 days, re-evaluate model’s baseline assumption and adjust for recent price momentum.",
    "In cases where true outcome exceeds forecast by >15% in the last 3-5 days, consider a ‘mean reversion’ correction: reduce forecast by 5-10% to align with recent trend reversal."
  ]
}
